definitions.meaning: staying cool and collected under pressure
written as music, as a composer scores a piece

explanation.definitionFit: Someone collected and serene is self-possessed, and a piece of music that has been written out has been created by a composer.

clue.text: Tom in trouble, goes to hospital department for something soothing

indicators.note: in trouble shows the cat's name and the little word after it are in disarray

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A tomcat in a scrape is taken to hospital for a balm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' turns TOM IN into OINTM; 'goes to' is a link joining ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A salve or balm rubbed into the skin eases soreness.

parts.note: playthings read as the things used in plays on stage, not toys

explanation.surface: A toy cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre, props used in the plays are stored in a dedicated store.

clue.text: Luggage sent up to a place in Greece

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: traps is an old word for personal belongings or baggage
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bags being shipped off to a Greek destination.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a famous city-state of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Late, but if on time, not late

definitions.meaning: deceased
in the phrase 'on time', exact and punctual

explanation.definitionFit: The late someone has died, and arriving precisely punctual is described as being exactly on time.

parts.note: not light in weight but used in electric lights, being the filament of bulbs; in fact it is very heavy

explanation.surface: A question about a metal of low weight, such as aluminium.
explanation.definitionFit: This very dense element makes the glowing filaments in incandescent bulbs.

clue.text: Place where economy of truth is fashionable

parts.note: a falsehood is being economical with the truth
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A venue where being sparing with honesty is the trend.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase recalls 'economical with the truth'; 'in lieu of' means in place of.
explanation.definitionFit: The word survives in 'in lieu of', meaning instead of, in the stead of.

clue.text: Symptoms of an extremely silly modern disorder

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters of silly
disorder says the letters of modern are jumbled

explanation.surface: Signs of some absurd contemporary ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives SY from silly; 'disorder' turns MODERN into NDROME.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndrome is a group of signs that together characterise a medical condition.

clue.text: Communist aim — end of private property?

definitions.text: Communist aim — end of private property?

parts.words: Communist aim — end of private property?
parts.note: abolishing private ownership is what communists hope will make everyone level with one another

explanation.surface: A political question about what communism is really after.
explanation.definitionFit: Communism seeks a society where nobody owns more than anybody else, so all stand level in wealth and status.

definitions.meaning: to unfasten or unwrap something
to bring about someone's ruin, as in 'pride was his downfall'

explanation.definitionFit: One unties a knot or parcel to open it, and a person who is ruined has been brought down or defeated.

parts.note: a private soldier is drilled here; the surface suggests a privately owned oil well

explanation.surface: Someone's own patch of land where an oil well is being sunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers, privates among them, march and practise drill on a large open square at the barracks.

clue.text: The position of one submitting — a proposal?

definitions.text: The position of one submitting — a proposal?

parts.words: The position of one submitting — a proposal?
parts.note: someone submitting kneels; a man proposing marriage traditionally does so too

explanation.surface: Someone putting forward a formal proposal for consideration.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneeling on one knee is the posture of supplication and the classic pose for asking for a hand in marriage.

indicators.note: perhaps tells the solver that the word Arrested is just one possible arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: A motorist is stopped by police and also gets the tyres replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Retreads are old tyres given a new tread moulded onto the worn casing, so they are re-covered rather than replaced.

definitions.meaning: resolved, bent on doing something
a scrap or brief bout of fighting

explanation.definitionFit: One resolved on a task is firmly intent on it, and a brief scrap or quarrel is a set-to.

clue.text: Pack luggage in to boot for Caribbean resort

indicators.note: the bag is packed in, placed inside the other word

parts.note: to boot means too, as well
a bag is a piece of luggage

explanation.surface: Advice to throw a suitcase into the car boot before a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' and 'in' together signal the container; 'to boot' is an idiom for as well. TOBAGO is the smaller island of Trinidad and Tobago.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a holiday island in the West Indies, popular with tourists.

definitions.meaning: to halt or restrain
a rope or wire bracing a ship's mast

explanation.definitionFit: A court can halt or suspend proceedings, and on a sailing ship a strong rope supporting the mast fore and aft has the same name.

clue.text: Not the main road from Spithead

indicators.note: from here signals that the letters are made out of the place name rearranged

explanation.surface: A minor route leading away from a naval anchorage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' turns SPITHEAD into SIDEPATH. Spithead is a stretch of water off Portsmouth used as a naval anchorage.
explanation.definitionFit: A side path is a minor track branching off a principal route.

clue.text: Assumed to be back in bed

indicators.note: to be back says the phrase for being in bed is read from end to start

parts.note: someone in bed is not up

explanation.surface: Someone presumed to have returned to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be back' turns NOT UP round, giving PUT ON. 'Assumed' here means adopted falsely, as an accent may be.
explanation.definitionFit: An affected accent or manner is feigned or donned for show, just as one may take on a false air.

clue.text: Get the kids to sleep and finish the paper

definitions.meaning: tuck children in for the night
printing jargon for completing an edition and sending it to press

explanation.definitionFit: Parents tuck children in at bedtime, and journalists finalise an issue of the newspaper ready for printing with the same phrase.

definitions.meaning: a single musical tone
to jot down or write down

explanation.definitionFit: A single musical tone is the basic unit of a melody, and to write something down briefly is to jot it.

definitions.meaning: the valve controlling fuel to an engine
to strangle

explanation.definitionFit: The valve regulating fuel to an engine governs speed, and to strangle someone is to grip the neck.

definitions.meaning: a boat hollowed out of a tree trunk
a covered trench or bunker, as for soldiers or a team's bench

explanation.definitionFit: A primitive boat is made by hollowing a log, and a roofed pit dug into the ground serves troops or football substitutes as cover.

clue.text: Route was changed, now lasts longer than others

indicators.note: changed shows the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diverted road that ends up being longer lasting than its rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns ROUTE WAS into OUTWEARS; 'now' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwear something is to survive or endure beyond it, remaining in use after it has worn out.

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of The

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was a French composer

explanation.surface: The opening composer to go on a concert tour.
explanation.definitionFit: To journey around a region is to make a trip through it.

parts.note: a line painted on a hull showing the deepest a vessel may safely sit in the water; the surface suggests a cautious shipping company

explanation.surface: A shipping company with a good safety record.
explanation.walkthrough: It is named after Samuel Plimsoll, the British MP who campaigned for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The load line on a merchant ship's side marks the limit to which it may be loaded and remain seaworthy.

indicators.note: of means the run of letters is taken from within the next word

explanation.surface: A historic base from which missionaries set out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early centre' is the definition: St Columba's monastery made this small island off western Scotland an early hub of Christianity. The run sits in the middle of 'missionaries', which tempts a cryptic-definition reading.
explanation.definitionFit: St Columba's sixth-century abbey on this Hebridean island was a cradle of Celtic Christianity.

clue.text: Reluctant to see the point dropped

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see

indicators.note: dropped says a letter falls out of the little word the

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to let a matter rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' takes E (east, a compass point) out of THE, leaving TH. LOTH is a variant spelling of loath.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a variant spelling of the adjective for being unwilling or disinclined.

definitions.meaning: enclosed practice pitches surrounded by mesh
traps, as a fisherman does

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket batters practise in mesh-sided practice lanes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket batsmen practise inside mesh enclosures, and a fisherman bags or traps fish.

indicators.note: about means the belief goes round the other piece

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief
men stands for mankind

explanation.surface: Someone clinging to a conviction about the human race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' is the legal sense: property held by tenure, such as a block of flats.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a tenement is land or property held by a tenant, so it is a possession held under tenure.

clue.text: Stop deer straying with ropes round their necks

parts.note: to stop is to halt

indicators.note: straying means the letters of deer wander out of order

explanation.surface: Halting wandering deer by roping them.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals fitted with head ropes or straps for leading them have been tethered at the neck.
